title: Spike: HTTPS on the deployment network
lead: Prove the chosen HTTPS approach works on a non-technical household member's actual phone, at home, without the VPN.
boundary: **Not in this slice:** the production container; anything beyond a hello-world page plus the PWA manifest.

sections.heading: Why
sections.body: docs/research/https-lan.md lists the inferences that only a real device can confirm: cert accepted on a LAN IP, DNS override not bypassed, PWA installable.

sections.heading: Owner input
sections.body:
1. A time when the owner and a household phone that isn't on the VPN are both available.
2. Approval for any DNS-provider token or Tailscale setting changes.

sections.heading: Files
sections.body:
- `deploy/spike/` (Caddyfile or proxy config used)
- `docs/research/https-lan.md` (results section)
- `docs/decisions/0021-reference-deployment.md` (Accepted or revised)

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body: None automated. The checklist below is the test.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
1. Stand up the reverse proxy on the chosen host with the chosen cert method, in front of `python -m larder` (or a static page with the manifest).
2. Add the local DNS override for the name → the host's LAN IP.
3. On a household phone that isn't on the VPN (home Wi-Fi, no VPN): open the URL; confirm no cert warning; confirm DNS resolves to the LAN IP.
4. Install to home screen; confirm it opens standalone.
5. On the owner's phone: confirm it works on the LAN, and away from home over the VPN.
6. Confirm renewal: how and when the cert renews; note the date to re-check.
7. Record the results; accept ADR 0021 or switch to the other candidate and repeat.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body:
- Every step above was recorded with pass/fail in the research doc.
- ADR 0021 is Accepted.

sections.heading: Git
sections.body: Commit only when the owner asks; no AI attribution.
